goal_results.title: Vision Dataset Leakage Audit

evidence.note: verify_completion.json originally scored this 'partial' (not 'met') because the minimum_viable clause's second half -- 'state a corrected, caveated headline vision number' -- was outstanding at verification time.
G5 RESOLUTION (option a): this audit's own new script, run against sure_models/sure_v1/weights/best.pt, closes the previously-open item.

goal_results.success_criteria_met: minimum_viable, now fully met including the previously-outstanding half. Strong criterion ('zero cross-split leakage beyond ogretmen') is NOT met: perceptual hashing (aHash+dHash, <=5-bit threshold) found 32 near-duplicate train/val pairs across videos 2/4/5/6/7 and frame_source0, 14 of them adjacent frame indices of the same source video (0 exact frame-index overlaps -- distinct from, and milder than, the already-corrected ogretmen exact-duplicate leak). Minimum_viable's first clause (enumerate affected files/videos) was already met by EXP05. Minimum_viable's second clause (state a corrected, caveated headline number) is met by THIS AUDIT: re-running model.val() on best.pt with the 13 val images touched by the 14 adjacent-index pairs excluded (85-image val set) gives P=0.852/R=0.712/mAP50=0.8345/mAP50-95=0.5877, vs. the unfiltered 98-image baseline (measured in this same session) P=0.859/R=0.719/mAP50=0.8395/mAP50-95=0.5952 -- a delta of -0.007/-0.007/-0.005/-0.007. A more conservative bound excluding all 17 val images touched by any of the 32 strict-threshold pairs (81-image val set) gives P=0.846/R=0.712/mAP50=0.8335/mAP50-95=0.5869 (delta -0.013/-0.007/-0.006/-0.008 vs baseline).
gaps: This is a same-checkpoint re-evaluation on a smaller val set, not a retrain on a re-split, clip-disjoint dataset -- it estimates the DIRECTION and rough MAGNITUDE of the leakage's optimistic bias (a small, real effect: roughly 0.5-1.3 points across metrics) but does not produce a fully leakage-free number, since the flagged val images' near-duplicate counterparts remain in the training set that produced best.pt's weights.

17-distinct-val-image exclusion (81 images) is itself an approximation of 'all leakage' -- the near-duplicate detection method (perceptual hash) has its own threshold sensitivity (32 hits at <=5 bits, 202 at <=10 bits, 902 at <=16 bits); a looser threshold would flag more images and likely show a larger, not smaller, corrected delta.
goal_results.confidence: high (that leakage exists and the correction direction is negative/small); medium (that this specific magnitude is the exact bias a full clip-disjoint re-split would show, since retraining on a corrected split -- not merely re-evaluating -- was out of scope)

goal_results.title: Export-Format Accuracy Loss: Mechanism and Reproducibility
goal_results.success_criteria_met: strong: six-configuration table reproduced with commit hash (3c1b9fa); CoreML/ANE latency measured across 3 independent process invocations, p50 9.03+/-0.22ms, p95 9.60+/-0.18ms (genuine multi-session variance, not a single sample); fresh model.val() confirms no new epoch-73-style discrepancy; new per-image ONNX-vs-TorchScript diff script finds 0/98 images meaningfully different, median matched-pair IoU 0.99999976 -- stronger direct evidence for the shared-post-processing-path claim than the design anticipated; sources 8/9 cited.
gaps: Near-bit-identical ONNX/TorchScript agreement confirms the two exports match EACH OTHER, but does not by itself isolate NMS specifically as the causal mechanism vs. other generic export-vs-eager numeric differences -- full isolation would need a pre-NMS raw-output comparison against pt/mps, explicitly out of scope and disclosed as such.
surprises: INT8 quantization (deltaMAP50=-0.0082) loses LESS accuracy than fp32 ONNX/TorchScript export (deltaMAP50=-0.0104) -- counter to a naive expectation that quantization should be the more lossy operation. See Emergent Findings.

goal_results.title: Vision Operating-Point Safety Trace
goal_results.success_criteria_met: strong: fish-per-frame distribution computed directly from val labels (min k=3, avg 15.56, matching MODEL_RAPORU's ~15.6); full-frame-miss rarity quantified both empirically (0/98 at deployed conf=0.20) and via an independence approximation (0.053 expected misses); confidence-threshold sweep confirms 0.858/0.719 is (within curve resolution, F1 delta 0.0008) the true F1-argmax; H7 stated with confident language per its OPEN/C7 novelty status; Known Limitations #2 text carried forward and traced to backend/rules.py's fish_count==0 rule.
gaps: The val set contains zero frames with k=1 or k=2 ground-truth fish -- the sparse-frame regime is untested, not merely rare (see Emergent Findings); the 21.8-28.1% extrapolated miss-risk at k=1 is an untested extrapolation from the independence approximation, never a measurement.
surprises: Ultralytics' `model.val(conf=X)` does not pin box.mp/box.mr to X -- it reports an argmax-over-the-retained-curve figure regardless of a low passed conf, a tooling trap that would silently mislead anyone trying to read P/R 'at' a specific low threshold this way.

The deployed operating point (conf=0.20) actually runs at P=0.720/R=0.782 -- materially different from, and more recall-favorable than, the headline academic-argmax P=0.858/R=0.719 the rest of the manuscript cites (see Emergent Findings).

goal_results.title: MLOps PSI Drift-Binning Systematic Sweep & Three-Way Gate Exercise
goal_results.success_criteria_met: minimum_viable fully met, both sub-clauses: (a) the sweep precisely reports where quantile-vs-equal-width does and does not separate cleanly -- quantile is MORE sensitive at delta<=0.06 (e.g. delta=0.02: 0.164 vs 0.078), the literal opposite of H5's naive wording, with equal-width only overtaking and becoming more explosive from delta>=0.08 onward (delta=0.30: 4.844 vs 7.649), mechanism confirmed via per-bin decomposition (one large fixed equal-width bin, holding 30.1% of reference mass, emptying); (b) the equal-width curve is explicitly and correctly labeled a reconstruction, not recovered history, since `git log --oneline --all -- mlops/drift.py` returns exactly 1 commit. The strong criterion's implicit qualitative-shape claim ('equal-width jumps early, quantile grades smoothly') is NOT confirmed as stated -- it is corrected, not confirmed. retrain.py's three-way decide() gate (no-drift->none PSI=0.0048; significant-drift->retrain PSI=0.9070) and the three-case gate() MIN_IMPROVEMENT exercise both behave exactly as designed, exceeding minimum_viable into most of the strong criterion.
gaps: Self-flagged internal inconsistency: the sweep table's own delta=0.04 entry (quantile PSI=0.7279) differs from the separately-drawn significant-drift window at the same nominal delta (PSI=0.9070), due to unseeded per-call resampling inside an otherwise fixed-seed script. No headline manuscript number depends on the exact value of either.
surprises: The direction of H5's core qualitative claim is inverted at low severities -- quantile binning is the MORE sensitive scheme in the 'moderate' band, not equal-width.

g5_open_item_resolution.rationale: Raw val-set labels (data/sure_dataset/val/{images,labels}) and the exact checkpoint used for all headline vision numbers (sure_models/sure_v1/weights/best.pt) are both present and directly usable with Ultralytics' existing model.val() -- no retraining, no new labeling, and no monkeypatching of production code was required. This makes a defensible, directly-computed corrected number strictly better evidence than a caveat sentence alone, and it was completed within this audit's own scope (a filtered val split built via symlinks in a scratch directory; sure-project's data/ and weights were never modified).
g5_open_item_resolution.method: Two exclusion sets were built from EXP05's exp05_summary.json strict_threshold_hits_detail (32 near-duplicate train/val pairs at <=5-bit aHash/dHash distance): (1) the 13 distinct val images touched by the 14 adjacent-frame-index pairs (the textbook temporal-adjacency leak pattern), giving an 85-image filtered val set; (2) the 17 distinct val images touched by all 32 strict-threshold pairs (a more conservative bound), giving an 81-image filtered val set. model.val() was re-run against sure_models/sure_v1/weights/best.pt for the unfiltered 98-image baseline and both filtered sets in the same session, using data/sure_dataset/train unchanged in every run (only val was filtered).
g5_open_item_resolution.recommended_manuscript_caveat_sentence: After excluding the 13-17 validation frames identified as near-duplicate (temporally adjacent) with training frames from the same source video, re-evaluation of the deployed checkpoint yields precision=0.846-0.852 / recall=0.712 / mAP50=0.8335-0.8345 (vs. the unfiltered headline 0.859/0.719/0.8395) -- a modest, quantified optimistic bias of roughly 0.5-1.3 points depending on the exclusion threshold used, smaller than the already-disclosed ogretmen exact-duplicate leak and not conclusion-changing, but real and now measured rather than merely flagged.
g5_open_item_resolution.caveat_sentence_still_required: Even with the corrected number in hand, this is a same-checkpoint re-evaluation on a smaller held-out set, not a retrain on a clip-disjoint re-split (the near-duplicate training frames themselves remain in the training set that produced best.pt) -- the manuscript should present the corrected numbers as a bias estimate, and note that a fully leakage-free number would require retraining on a re-split dataset, which remains future work.

emergent_findings.title: AQUA-1B fabricates specific numeric sensor values inside otherwise-correctly-labeled reasoning
emergent_findings.description: 6 of 8 eval.py scenarios contain a free-text reasoning string with a fabricated sensor value that does not match the actual input snapshot (e.g. claiming DO=6.0 mg/L when the actual reading was 5.7 or 7.8) -- in 2 of those cases (T05, T08) the model reaches the categorically correct final status via an entirely invented causal narrative. This is invisible to apply_rule_override, rule_based_decision, and the four-bucket classification itself, all of which compare only the enumerable status field, never reasoning content.
emergent_findings.not_a_restatement_of: G3's planned deliverable was to find >=1 non-enumerable failure mode illustrating H2's scope boundary; the specific mechanism found (fabrication surviving inside the 'agrees' bucket) and its rate (6/8, not merely 1) were not predicted in research_goals.json or experiment_design.json.

emergent_findings.title: A stale, superseded detection-recall figure (0.695) is live inside the production RAG knowledge base
emergent_findings.description: llm-service/knowledge/06-davranis-ve-refah-gostergeleri.md:58 states recall as '~0.695' (the incorrect epoch-73 figure) as a live fact. This file is ingested by llm-service/rag/ingest.py into the production pgvector store, making the stale number retrievable and potentially surfaceable verbatim by the deployed LLM -- a live data-integrity bug distinct from (and more severe than) the already-known, self-flagged-stale TODOS.md occurrence. emergent_findings.not_a_restatement_of: G11's planned deliverable was a grep pass confirming 0.695 does not ship in the manuscript; finding a live leak inside a production data source (not a manuscript artifact) was an unplanned discovery of the grep's own scope.

emergent_findings.title: Vision recall has two both-correct, materially different numbers depending on the question asked
emergent_findings.description: The headline academic F1-argmax operating point is P=0.858/R=0.719, but the actual deployed system (yolo_runner.py, CONF_THRESH=0.20) runs at P=0.720/R=0.782 -- a substantially higher-recall, lower-precision point, deliberately chosen (per an inline code comment) to reduce misses on crowded frames. The manuscript, prior to this pipeline, had no language distinguishing which number governs the H7 safety discussion; 0.782, not 0.719, is the number that actually governs real-world full-frame-miss risk, and it is the MORE reassuring of the two.
emergent_findings.not_a_restatement_of: G7's planned deliverable was to confirm 0.858/0.719 as the F1-argmax (which it does); discovering that this argmax point is NOT the deployed operating point, and that Ultralytics' val(conf=X) will not reveal this by naive use, was an unplanned methodological and substantive finding.

emergent_findings.title: The validation set contains zero sparse frames (k=1 or k=2 fish) -- the safety-relevant regime is untested, not merely rare
emergent_findings.description: All 98 val images have k>=3 ground-truth fish (min=3, avg=15.56). The design phase's hypothesis worried about a 'materially sparse subset' of frames; no such frames exist to check. The reassuring empirical 0/98 full-frame-miss result therefore says nothing about the sparse-frame regime, where the independence-approximation extrapolated miss-risk is highest (21.8-28.1% at k=1, untested).
emergent_findings.not_a_restatement_of: This is a dataset-coverage gap discovered while computing G7's planned fish-per-frame distribution, not a result G7 was designed to produce -- verification_results.json's own reviewer explicitly flagged it as a 7th, newly-added Known Limitations item beyond EXP11's original 6.

emergent_findings.title: AQUA-7B's agentic-benchmark format-compliance and step-count figures do not reproduce from a fresh, code-unmodified run
emergent_findings.description: A fresh re-run of bench_agent.py against AQUA-7B measures 100% format compliance and 2.0 mean steps, vs. the published README's 60% format / 3.6 mean steps -- selection% and the constant-answer conclusion reproduce exactly, but format%/step-count do not, with no configuration difference (adapter path, PLAN_MAX_TOKENS, MAX_STEPS) found to explain the gap. Most likely cause: undocumented mlx-lm / model-serving-stack version drift between whenever the original README table was produced and this run.
emergent_findings.not_a_restatement_of: G4's planned deliverable was to reproduce the existing figures and grow the scenario count; an unexplained partial non-reproduction of a previously-published number is a genuinely unplanned reproducibility finding, independently reconfirmed in EXP11's provenance audit (item 4 of its 6-item stale-figure list).

emergent_findings.title: INT8 quantization loses LESS accuracy than fp32 ONNX/TorchScript export
emergent_findings.description: The INT8-quantized ONNX export has deltaMAP50=-0.0082, smaller in magnitude than the fp32 ONNX/TorchScript exports' deltaMAP50=-0.0104 -- counter to the naive expectation that a lower-precision, more aggressively optimized export format should lose more accuracy, not less. Consistent with GitHub-issue-thread reports (source 8) that export/NMS-path mismatches, not weight precision, dominate small-model detection accuracy loss at export time.
emergent_findings.not_a_restatement_of: G6's planned deliverable was to reproduce the six-configuration table and test the shared-post-processing-path causal claim for the fp32 formats; the INT8-vs-fp32 ordering itself is a secondary, counter-intuitive pattern surfaced by reading the full table, not something G6's hypothesis (H6) specifically predicted or was designed to detect.
